title: US Sanctions ICC President Tomoko Akane as Washington Escalates Court Campaign, Seoul Cuts Drills by Half
subhead: The Trump administration sanctioned the International Criminal Court's president and a senior trial lawyer, deepening its campaign against the Hague-based court, while the US and South Korea slashed their annual joint exercise at Trump's direction and Gaza's restricted areas expanded to nearly two-thirds of the territory.

sections.heading: US Sanctions ICC Leadership in Escalating Court Campaign
sections.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced sanctions on Tuesday against ICC President Tomoko Akane of Japan and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal, according to the US Treasury Department and Middle East Eye. Rubio accused the court of being a corrupt and politicized institution that has abused its authority and assaulted state sovereignty by targeting officials from non-member states. The move follows an executive order from President Trump targeting the court last year and comes on top of sanctions already imposed on at least 11 ICC officials, including nine judges and the chief prosecutor, per BBC reporting.

The sanctions target the court's most senior figure for the first time. Akane, a Japanese judge who became ICC president in 2024, and Seye are now subject to US financial restrictions for what Rubio described as efforts to investigate, arrest, or prosecute officials whose governments have not consented to ICC jurisdiction. The court, empowered by more than 120 member countries to investigate war crimes, has been a persistent target of the Trump administration.
sections.whyItMatters: Sanctioning the sitting ICC president is a direct escalation of Washington's effort to dismantle a court that has pursued cases against US allies and non-member states, signaling that the administration will not tolerate ICC jurisdiction over American personnel or partners.

sections.heading: US and South Korea Cut Ulchi Freedom Shield by Nearly Half
sections.body:
South Korea and the United States agreed to shorten their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise, ending it Friday instead of the originally scheduled August 27, at the request of President Trump, Yonhap reported. The allies will complete the first, defensive phase of the exercise this week and cancel the second phase involving counter-attack operations, according to the South China Morning Post. Field training will also be reduced, with the Combined Forces Command operating out of two separate command posts at the wartime CP Tango bunker in Seongnam and at Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek.

Trump called for substantially scaling down the drills in a social media post on Sunday, citing cost and his relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The Pentagon said the adjustments preserve essential readiness with no degradation to training objectives. US Forces Korea Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson made an unannounced visit to Seoul's defense ministry to meet Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back as the schedule was adjusted.
sections.whyItMatters: Halving the flagship US-South Korea exercise and dropping its counter-attack phase is a concrete concession to Pyongyang that weakens the allies' demonstrated deterrent posture, even as North Korea denounced the drills.

sections.heading: Gaza Restricted Areas Expand to 64.9 Percent Since Ceasefire
sections.body:
Since the Gaza ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, Israeli military operations have continued, more than 1,200 Palestinians have been killed and restricted areas have expanded to 64.9 percent of the territory, according to figures reported by the United Nations from Gaza's Health Ministry and analysis by Daily News Egypt. Al Jazeera reports at least 1,265 people killed in the enclave since the ceasefire came into effect. The second phase of the agreement, intended to pave the way for a political settlement, remains stalled as international attention shifted to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The ceasefire reduced the intensity of fighting but did not end the conflict: Israel did not fully withdraw, and the next political phase was never meaningfully implemented. The territory sits in an ambiguous state between reduced fighting and entrenched changes on the ground, with the US stance on demilitarization and rising West Bank violence complicating any path forward.
sections.whyItMatters: The expansion of restricted areas to nearly two-thirds of Gaza shows the ceasefire has become a vehicle for consolidating Israeli control rather than a step toward a political settlement, with the second phase of the agreement effectively frozen.

sections.heading: Ghana Reports 62 Citizens Killed in Ukraine War as Minister Presses Moscow
sections.body:
Ghana's Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said 62 Ghanaians have been killed and 15 remain missing in Russia's war against Ukraine, disclosing the figures during bilateral talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow, per MyJoyOnline and Ukrainska Pravda. Ablakwa said Ghana was particularly concerned about the recruitment of young Ghanaians lured to Russia under various circumstances before being enlisted to fight. Lavrov said Russia will consider Ghana's requests regarding its citizens in the Russian armed forces, noting similar requests have come from other countries.

The minister said the two sides agreed to work together to stop the illegal recruitment of Ghanaians, and that Ghana would continue diplomatic and advocacy efforts to disrupt recruitment networks. The disclosure highlights the growing human cost of foreign recruitment into the conflict, with African nationals among those drawn into the fighting.
sections.whyItMatters: The confirmed deaths of 62 Ghanaian citizens in the Ukraine war underscores the scale of foreign recruitment into the conflict and gives African states a direct stake in pressing Moscow over the treatment of their nationals.

sections.heading: Hormuz Standoff Deepens as Trump Labels Strait 'New US Territory'
sections.body:
President Trump posted a map on Truth Social labeling the Strait of Hormuz as 'NEW U.S. Territory,' drawing a circle that also takes in a portion of mainland Iranian territory on the northern shore, per MercoPress. The post carried no accompanying text, but Trump had trailed the idea on Friday, saying, 'After we finish defeating Iran... pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.' He added, 'We have the blockade — no ships get through unless we want them to.'

Iran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, responded that 'The Strait of Hormuz cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order.' The 14-point US-Iran ceasefire memorandum of understanding expired on August 17 with no extension agreed, and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran has not decided whether to restart negotiations. Kpler data showed no vessels passed through the waterway on Sunday, compared with 31 a week earlier, while the USS Abraham Lincoln's deployment has extended to nearly 250 days amid a crew crisis that senators are pressing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to address.
sections.whyItMatters: With the ceasefire MoU expired and no formal talks scheduled, Trump's territorial claim and the naval blockade keep the world's most critical oil chokepoint shut and the risk of renewed conflict high.

bottomLine: Washington escalated its campaign against the International Criminal Court by sanctioning its sitting president, a first, while simultaneously cutting the US-South Korea exercise nearly in half at Trump's direction — two moves that signal a more aggressive posture toward international institutions and a more conciliatory one toward Pyongyang. In Gaza, restricted areas have grown to 64.9 percent of the territory since the ceasefire, showing the truce has hardened rather than reversed Israeli control. Ghana's disclosure that 62 of its citizens have been killed in Ukraine highlights the war's widening human toll, while the expired US-Iran ceasefire and Trump's claim over Hormuz leave the world's key oil chokepoint shut and the risk of renewed conflict high.
